angle: WR/TE break mechanics from Combine route drills (Break G: how hard a receiver pushes off the ground around his cut), graded with the same code on NFL snaps of the same route families, tested against full-season separation over expected (SOE) on held-out draft classes; positive use: last season's route-shrunk SOE as a day-3 tiebreaker, and break-phase speed traces as a film/coaching cue.
metric_name: Break G: mean acceleration (g) over the 1.0 s centred on the sharpest point of the first route break, z-scored within drill and Combine year and averaged over route drills; 1 sd = sd of true receiver Break G (0.021 g).
headline_number: Primary: -1.2 in of season SOE per sd of Break G [-3.6, +1.0], n=116 on unseen classes; same-route-family errors-in-variables true correlation 0.02 [-0.27, 0.32], P(>0.2)=17%. Day-3 SOE tiebreaker: leave-one-receiver-out rank-correlation gain 0.63 [-0.08, 0.90] (interval includes 0; flattered by a negative left-out baseline), all rounds 0.68 [0.14, 0.90]; no pick-by-SOE interaction (0.11 [-0.35, 0.57]).
what_changed_from_previous: Revision of round_15/cand_2 per judges. Data science: nested day-3 test (all 53 pairs pooled, receiver random intercept with pick x SOE interaction, leave-one-receiver-out gains with receiver-clustered intervals that redo the loop, shuffle null band); route-family hierarchical errors-in-variables Gibbs model with random family slopes (399 receiver-family cells), forest in Fig 2C with P(true link > 0.2); Platt recalibration fitted on held-out pairs, recalibrated probabilities printed in the 2026 table (cross-fitted day-3 forecast 41% vs 40% observed); catch conversion with bounds (7.0-10.7 catch-rate pts/yd, 43-84 targets); Break G sd stated in g. Football: one verdict sentence that the day-3 edge is not statistically distinguished (CI includes 0, 1 of 2 folds, 7 vs 6 of 13); cryptic 'passes over 7 pairs' line removed; worked contrast is now Boutte (hard cutter) vs Washington (soft) at picks 187/184, chosen by drill not forecast, with QB, man share, games, contracts and catch bounds, plus the median matched-pair gap (30 pts) so it is not presented as typical; § mark for Combine-discounted (NGS below class average); QB and man% columns; new Fig 3 film cue (speed at the top of NFL hitches, 2.0 vs 0.9 yd/s). Price-vs-value figure and survivorship detail moved out of the main text; 9% (beyond position) vs 14% (beyond 40/weight/NGS, earlier rounds) reconciled. Writeup: 6-word title, 45-word lede without intervals, coach definition of Break G, shuffle p/Brier/selection/mixed details to appendix, 'Firm' relabelled; text rendered from writeup_template.md by render.py so every number comes from the script. Viz: Fig 1 larger paths, 10.5 pt readouts, fixed-scale speed traces with brake/through/drive shading, on-figure selected-extremes badge, dumbbell removed; Fig 2C is the posterior forest in neutral colours; Fig 4 single-scale panel B with shuffle null bands, enlarged C with per-bin intervals and the recalibration curve, rows labelled by pair.
open_risks: Day-3 edge is still not proven: leave-one-receiver-out interval includes 0 and the gain is flattered by a negative left-out pick-and-routes baseline (-0.43)
Family model is a bounded null: P(true link > 0.2) is 17% pooled and up to 27% for one family, so a modest link is not ruled out
The film cue rests on six sampled NFL hitches per player, half of the sample selected for high EPA
Worked contrast is chosen by drill and pick, but it is the most divergent kind of pair; the median matched gap (30 points) is reported
Not a blind test; the 2026 class is the first true out-of-sample score; Combine-discounted mark is a simple NGS-below-average rule
